name: Viktor, Herald of the Arcane
howItPlays: You spend a turn's energy to exhaust Viktor and drop a small Recruit token onto an empty battlefield, using those cheap bodies to claim ground your opponent left open rather than to fight. You hold removal and stun spells for whatever real threat your opponent commits, answering it before it can hurt you and slowly turning empty battlefields into points.
whyYou: You like keeping problems small before they get big, holding your removal until your opponent actually plays something worth answering. Making a token to grab an empty battlefield feels better to you than swinging in for a risky trade, and you're happy watching a long game tip your way one careful answer at a time. If patience and clean removal feel more satisfying than racing, Viktor is for you.
ratingNotes: pace 2: riftbound.gg calls Viktor 'an off-tempo type of legend, designed to answer opposing threat, but also score points through conquering battlefield as often as possible', and its Recruit tokens are used 'to conquer empty battlefields' rather than to fight, a slow, methodical plan rather than a race. stance 2.5: the same guide says the deck is 'designed to answer opposing threat' first, relying on 'timely removal, stun, or might manipulation'; the token generation adds a small proactive edge (grabbing empty battlefields) but the identity is reactive. complexity 7.5: deciding when to spend Energy 1 to make a Recruit versus holding it for removal, and which cheap bodies to sacrifice or replace, is a genuine ongoing puzzle; the deck archetypes primer places Viktor in the Control camp, which that site treats as its most demanding category. variance 3: token generation and removal are repeatable rather than build-around, and a mono-Order manabase is possible, so games play out similarly turn to turn; hextechanalytics doesn't flag any swingy payoff card. Legend ability: pay Energy 1 and exhaust Viktor to play a 1 Might Recruit unit token. Confidence: medium, four sources found but one (the mono-Order guide) calls the deck 'aggressive' in isolation, contradicting the other three; went with the majority reactive/control read. Reviewer should double check the mono-Order build isn't actually the more common one in current results.
